titleText.es: La batería de un portátil contiene más o menos la energía de una granada de mano, y si la cortocircuitas... ¡Oye! ¡No puedes arrestarme solo por demostrar que vuestras leyes son inconsistentes!
titleText.en: A laptop battery contains roughly the stored energy of a hand grenade, and if shorted it ... hey!  You can't arrest me if I prove your rules inconsistent!

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Preocupados describes more than one masculine person or a mixed group. A feminine group uses preocupadas.

example.es: Mis vecinos están preocupados por el humo.
example.en: My neighbors are worried about the smoke.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: about; required after preocupado before the cause of concern
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish normally uses por after preocupado, preocupada, preocupados, or preocupadas to introduce what causes the worry.

example.en: We are worried about the exam.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Bomba can also mean a pump. Here the plural refers specifically to explosive devices.

example.es: Los artificieros retiraron dos bombas antiguas.
example.en: The bomb squad removed two old bombs.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you all let; you all allow (informal, mainly Spain)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Dejáis is the present form of dejar used with vosotros or vosotras. In this use, the person being allowed acts next.

example.en: Are you all letting the children enter?

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Meter describes placing something inside a container, space, or situation.

example.es: Mete la carta en el sobre.
example.en: Put the letter in the envelope.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: I subject; I expose (something to a condition)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Someto is the present form of someter used with yo. The thing affected normally comes before a, and the test or condition comes after a.

example.en: I subject the sample to pressure.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to; required after someter before the condition
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In someter algo a una prueba o condición, a introduces the test, force, or condition applied to the affected thing.

example.es: Sometieron el motor a varias pruebas.
example.en: They subjected the engine to several tests.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Rompo is the irregular present form of romper used with yo.

example.en: I break the seal carefully.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In a battery, a celda is one electrochemical unit. The same word can mean other kinds of enclosed cells in different contexts.

example.en: The battery contains six cells.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Provocaría keeps the full verb provocar and adds -ía to describe a conditional result.

example.en: An error would cause another delay.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here considerable describes something notably large rather than merely worthy of consideration.

example.es: El arreglo requiere una cantidad considerable.
example.en: The repair requires a substantial amount.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins en seguida, “right away”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: En and seguida work together as the time expression en seguida.

example.en: I will call you right away.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: right away; immediately (as part of en seguida)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In this fixed expression, seguida does not describe a feminine noun. The one-word spelling enseguida is also standard.

example.en: We will be right back.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; marks darse cuenta, “to realize”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Before a changed form of dar, se marks that one other person or thing—or formal usted—is the one who realizes something in the expression darse cuenta.

example.es: Ella se dio cuenta del error.
example.en: She realized the mistake.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: will realize (as part of se dará cuenta)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Dará is the future form of dar. With se and cuenta, it belongs to the fixed expression for realizing rather than meaning that someone will give something.

example.en: She will realize tomorrow.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Devolverá is the future form used with él, ella, or formal usted.

example.en: Marta will return the book tomorrow.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone is worried about something?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of estar, the matching form of preocupado, then por and the cause.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Estar changes for the person and time. Preocupado changes its ending to match whom it describes: preocupado, preocupada, preocupados, or preocupadas. Por remains unchanged before the source of concern.

example.es: Lucía está preocupada por su perro.
example.en: Lucía is worried about her dog.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: someter algo a + prueba o condición
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something is subjected to a test, force, or condition?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of someter, name or replace the affected thing, then use a before the test or condition.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Someter changes for the person and time. The affected thing can be named with a noun or replaced by a short word such as lo or la. The preposition a stays unchanged before what is applied to it.

example.es: Sometieron la tela a mucho calor.
example.en: They subjected the fabric to intense heat.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you reassure someone that there is no problem or that something is okay?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The expression literally uses pasar and nada, but it conventionally reassures someone that nothing bad is happening or that a mistake does not matter.

example.en: —Sorry for arriving late. —No problem.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something happens right away?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use en seguida, meaning “right away” or “immediately.”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: En seguida is a fixed two-word time expression. The one-word spelling enseguida has the same meaning and is also standard.

example.en: The doctor will come right away.

applications.explanationEn: Estáis matches the people addressed, preocupados describes that plural group, and por introduces las bombas as the source of concern.
The -áis ending marks the several people addressed informally in the vosotros form used mainly in Spain.
The two-word accented form por qué introduces this direct question asking for a reason.
Me identifies the person receiving permission, dejáis matches the people allowing it, and meter stays in its unchanged dictionary form as the allowed action.
The -áis ending marks the several people addressed informally in the vosotros form used mainly in Spain.
La replaces the affected battery, someto is the speaker's form of someter, and a introduces sobrevoltaje as the applied condition.
Provocaría keeps the full verb provocar and adds -ía to present the explosion as a conditional result.
Considerable follows explosión in the common neutral order for a description.
Considerable is singular to match singular explosión and has the same singular form with masculine and feminine nouns.

applications.explanationEn: The complete fixed expression reassures the listener that the alarming situation is not a problem.
En seguida places the expected realization in the immediate future.
Se matches the person expected to realize something, dará supplies the future form of dar, cuenta completes the expression, and de que opens the fact to be recognized.
Dará keeps the dictionary form dar and adds -á for a future action by one other person or thing.
Tengo matches the speaker, and razón completes the conventional expression for claiming to be right.
Devolverá keeps the dictionary form devolver and adds -á for a future action by one other person or thing.
Agua remains feminine, but its initial stressed a sound makes singular el the article used immediately before it.
